questions.explain: DTU is a blended measure of CPU, memory, and I/O bundled into one number whose components you cannot see or control; if the bottleneck is I/O but you're buying a CPU-heavy tier, you pay for resources you don't consume — and DTU blocks Hybrid Benefit.
options: DTU is a blended measure of CPU, memory, and I/O you cannot observe or control, so you can pay for the wrong resources — and DTU databases cannot use Azure Hybrid Benefit
DTU tiers always cost more than vCore for the same workload
DTU does not support auto-pause
DTU is only available in the Basic tier
questions.q: What is the core cost problem with the DTU purchasing model?

questions.explain: The chapter shows a GP 4 vCore (Gen5) at ~$368/month PAYG dropping to ~$186 with Hybrid Benefit and ~$155 with a 1-year RI on top — the two discounts stack and require no code changes.
options: Only reserved instances — Hybrid Benefit cannot be combined with them
Only the Azure Hybrid Benefit — reserved capacity requires Enterprise Agreement
Both stack: Hybrid Benefit plus a 1-year reserved instance take a GP 4 vCore from ~$368 to ~$155/month
Neither; discounts apply only to Business Critical tier
questions.q: For a General Purpose 4 vCore database, which discounts combine to reach ~$155/month from ~$368/month pay-as-you-go?

questions.explain: The chapter's decision framework says Serverless fits databases used fewer than 12 hours/day that tolerate a 30–90 second cold start, and the break-even between Serverless and provisioned vCore is roughly 50% average utilization across a 730-hour month.
options: Workloads above 80% average utilization with predictable load
Databases used fewer than ~12 hours/day that tolerate a 30–90 second cold start — break-even is ~50% average monthly utilization
Any database over 4 TB
Only databases in elastic pools
questions.q: When does the chapter recommend Azure SQL Serverless over provisioned vCore?

questions.explain: Microsoft's rough guideline is 100 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for Standard/General Purpose and 125 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for Premium/Business Critical — e.g., P2 (250 DTU, ~$930/month) maps to a GP 8 vCore at ~$736 PAYG, or ~$310 with Hybrid Benefit and a 1-year RI.
options: 50 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for all tiers
250 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for Standard; 100 DTUs for Premium
100 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for Standard/General Purpose; 125 DTUs ≈ 1 vCore for Premium/Business Critical
DTUs cannot be converted to vCores; you must re-provision and migrate data
questions.q: What is Microsoft's rough DTU-to-vCore conversion guideline used in the chapter?

questions.explain: The chapter warns that In-Memory OLTP (MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON tables) is supported in DTU Premium but not in vCore General Purpose — such databases must migrate to Business Critical, not General Purpose.
options: Databases using In-Memory OLTP (memory-optimized tables) must go to Business Critical, because General Purpose does not support it
Databases over 32 GB must stay on DTU
Databases with auto-pause enabled cannot migrate to vCore
Databases using TDE cannot migrate to vCore
